_help: The Reporting verb bank page. Each verb has a pattern and two examples: "present" and "past". The app shows the example that matches the reportingVerbTense setting in config.js ("either" shows both).

groups.title: Tentative
groups.about: The author is careful or not completely sure. Use these for ideas that still need testing.

verbs.present: Petrova (2021) suggests that shorter lectures might help students concentrate.
verbs.past: Petrova (2021) suggested that shorter lectures might help students concentrate.

verbs.pattern: propose + noun phrase, or propose + that-clause
verbs.present: Volkov (2023) proposes a new way to plan bike lanes in small towns.
verbs.past: Volkov (2023) proposed a new way to plan bike lanes in small towns.

verbs.present: Tran (2019) hypothesises that bilingual children switch tasks more easily.
verbs.past: Tran (2019) hypothesised that bilingual children switch tasks more easily.

verbs.present: Romano (2020) speculates that printed books may become a luxury.
verbs.past: Romano (2020) speculated that printed books may become a luxury.

groups.title: Neutral
groups.about: The author presents information without a strong opinion.

verbs.present: Nakamura (2020) states that campus housing is full.
verbs.past: Nakamura (2020) stated that campus housing was full.

verbs.pattern: report + that-clause, or report + noun phrase
verbs.present: Nakamura (2020) reports the number of students living on campus.
verbs.past: Nakamura (2020) reported the number of students living on campus.

verbs.present: As Zhou (2023) notes, noise is a common problem in shared houses.
verbs.past: As Zhou (2023) noted, noise is a common problem in shared houses.

verbs.present: Achieng (2018) describes how student loans are paid back.
verbs.past: Achieng (2018) described how student loans are paid back.

verbs.pattern: explain + that-clause, or explain + how / why …
verbs.present: Lindqvist (2017) explains why green roofs keep buildings cool.
verbs.past: Lindqvist (2017) explained why green roofs keep buildings cool.

verbs.present: Varga (2014) outlines three ways to review lecture notes.
verbs.past: Varga (2014) outlined three ways to review lecture notes.

groups.title: Strong
groups.about: The author holds a firm position. Use these for opinions and arguments, not for research results.

verbs.present: Haddad (2019) argues that cities need more green space.
verbs.past: Haddad (2019) argued that cities needed more green space.

verbs.pattern: claim + that-clause. Careful: “claim” can suggest that you doubt the author.
verbs.present: Moreau (2019) claims that reading for pleasure helps in every subject.
verbs.past: Moreau (2019) claimed that reading for pleasure helps in every subject.

verbs.present: Castillo (2018) asserts that confidence grows when students are allowed to make mistakes.
verbs.past: Castillo (2018) asserted that confidence grows when students are allowed to make mistakes.

verbs.present: Moretti (2017) maintains that homework should be banned in primary schools.
verbs.past: Moretti (2017) maintained that homework should be banned in primary schools.

groups.title: Findings
groups.about: The author has evidence from research: an experiment, a survey or data.

verbs.present: Duarte (2022) finds that most students prefer printed books for long texts.
verbs.past: Duarte (2022) found that most students preferred printed books for long texts.

verbs.pattern: show + that-clause, or show + noun phrase
verbs.present: Tran (2020) shows that bilingual children switch tasks faster.
verbs.past: Tran (2020) showed that bilingual children switched tasks faster.

verbs.pattern: demonstrate + that-clause, or demonstrate + noun phrase
verbs.present: Abebe et al. (2022) demonstrate that refill stations reduce plastic waste.
verbs.past: Abebe et al. (2022) demonstrated that refill stations reduced plastic waste.

notes: “According to Haddad (2019), …” already reports the idea. Do not add a reporting verb: NOT “According to Haddad (2019) argues that …”.
describe, discuss and outline take a noun phrase: “discussed the effects”, NOT “discussed about the effects” or “discussed that …”.
One author takes a singular verb (argues, has argued). Two authors and et al. take a plural verb (argue, have argued).
